candidates.title: The illuminated Apple logo returns on the new OLED MacBook Pro after about ten years
candidates.claim: New MacBook Pro with OLED display (announced 28 Oct 2026) brings back the glowing rear Apple logo, dropped with the 2016 MacBook Pro redesign (12-inch MacBook 2015 first). Brightness follows display brightness. Apple's own release/product/spec pages do not mention it; Apple has not explained why it was removed.
candidates.verification: verified by MacRumors (two articles, incl. hands-on video by UrAvgConsumer), Appleosophy, 9to5Mac, AppleInsider, Cult of Mac headlines; John Ternus post 'We're glowing with excitement' quoted by MacRumors. Apple newsroom fetch failed; blakecrosley.com notes Apple's pages don't mention the logo.
candidates.note: Strongest concrete image (a lit mark facing the room). Pair with C2 for the story.

candidates.title: Apple's laptop logo once faced the user (upside down to the room) and was flipped to face onlookers
candidates.claim: On early PowerBook/iBook, the logo read right-way-up to the user with lid closed, so upside down to everyone else when open. Users kept opening from the wrong side; Jobs first put the user first, later reversed so the logo faces the room. Moreno: wrong-side opening is a brief self-correcting annoyance; an upside-down logo to onlookers lasts.
candidates.verification: verified: Engadget (2012-05-21), CNN (2012-05-22), Daring Fireball link; single original source = Joe Moreno's blog (ex-Apple). Present as 'a former Apple employee recounted'.
candidates.note: Evergreen backbone of the chosen topic.

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: C1 confirmed by several Apple-news outlets the same day plus a hands-on video, but NOT on Apple's own pages: say 'reported on the new MacBook Pro', never quote Apple. Apple never explained the 2016 removal: do not invent a reason (no 'to make it thinner'). C2 rests on one ex-employee's account (Joe Moreno), widely reported in 2012: frame as 'a former Apple employee recounted'. Don't say 'Jobs said'. No sales/impact numbers exist for the glowing logo.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Visible consumption / badge effect: people buy partly for how a thing reads to others; the user rarely sees the logo, the room always does. A tiny design decision (which way up, lit or not) reveals who a brand mark is really for. Strong 'I never noticed that' moment (upside-down logo) = save/share trigger for both Persian and English viewers; Apple is globally familiar.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Identity + consumer behaviour: fits Behnood's brand-strategy voice. Owner takeaway for cafés, bakeries, salons, shops: your mark spends most of its life in your customer's hand, on the street, in photos — design the cup, the bag, the sleeve, the receipt for the people who are NOT your customer yet. Avoids the price topic of the last two days; different from 2026-11-02 (Apple Music) because the brand is the device maker and the idea is direction/visibility, not colour — do not reference the Apple Music reel.

gates.brand_fit_gate: C1+C2 pass; C3 fails (repeat of pricing/trust), C4 fails (repeat of effort), C12 fails (repeat of naming), C8/C9 fail (platform/media, not brand).
gates.story_gate: C1+C2: central tension = 'the user or the room?'; concrete image = a lit logo on a laptop lid facing a dark café; upside-down logo is a built-in twist. Beats C5 (stronger evergreen but no single image or news spark).

supporting: C5 (optional: product shapes are the most distinctive brand assets, 31% gold vs 4% for colours; Ipsos x JKR 2023)
decision.why: Fresh news spark + verified evergreen story + a universal owner lesson; works equally in Persian and English.
